title: analysis_config schema v2
description: Separates learned model architecture from observed runtime trace instances. schema_version=2. Legacy v1 configs migrated to v2 carry migration.status=legacy_unverified. `additionalProperties: false` here and on every nested object is load-bearing: `parallel_siblings` was read by a downstream consumer while being absent from this schema, so it could be neither required nor validated, and any misspelled field passed silently. A field that matters must be declared. `trace_instances` is NOT required -- a source-only decomposition is a complete artifact, since the architecture comes from the source and a capture only corroborates it; requiring instances forced source-only analyses to fabricate a capture record.

predicate.description: The source-level condition that puts a layer in this group, e.g. `layer_idx < first_k_dense_replace (3)`. Emitted by the adapters; declared here because closing this object without it would reject every manifest-derived config.

learned_module_count.description: Learned modules, NOT invocations. An MTP module invoked twice per step is 1 learned layer; conflating the two double-counts its parameters.

count_config_key.description: The config key this count was read from. Emitted by the adapters.

trace_scope.description: OPTIONAL, and describes only the capture it came from. The architecture is never derived from it, and its absence is not a defect. Retained for compatibility with existing configs; consumers must tolerate it being missing.

parallelism.description: Detected parallel sizes; each may be an integer or "unknown". Deliberately open: unlike every other object here, the set of parallel dimensions is not fixed (`world_size`, `attn_tp`, `moe_ep` all appear in real runtime YAMLs), and a closed list would reject the next backend's spelling. Every value is an annotation on the capture, never architecture, so an unrecognised key cannot corrupt the decomposition.

trace_instances.description: One record per observed runtime invocation of a repeated module (decoder layer, MTP iteration, etc.).

execution_profiles.description: Deployment configurations of this same source. Optional: a model with one entrypoint and no config-gated branches needs none.

deviations.description: Places where the AST cannot determine the dataflow (control flow on runtime tensor values, reflection, externally-generated graphs) and a human decided what the run actually does. Required for every blocking `unsupported` the extractor reports: check D5 fails without one, so the gap is declared rather than silently assumed away.

resolution.description: Which path this deployment takes, and the evidence for it.

model_flow.description: Ordered top-level node ids forming the whole-model chain, read by build_architecture_graph.py to connect embedding -> decoder stack -> tail. A LINEAR chain only: it cannot express a fork, a join, a cache read or an MTP re-entry, so `dataflow` below supersedes it for anything that is not a single path. Kept because existing configs and the downstream consumer use it.

dataflow.description: Explicit whole-model dataflow graph. OPTIONAL: `branches` already carries the intra-structure edges that the source can prove, and this is for edges that cross structure boundaries (embedding -> blocks -> head, MTP re-entry, KV cache reads) which have no other home. Supersedes `model_flow`, which can only express a linear chain. Nothing downstream may infer a top-level edge from node ordering, so an absent graph means those edges are undeclared, never that the model is a single chain.

nodes.description: Addressable endpoints for edges. Every edge endpoint must appear here (checked by check_dataflow, since JSON Schema cannot express a cross-reference).

structure.description: Key in `structures`/`stages` this node stands for, when it stands for one.

role.description: Free-form on purpose: a closed enum would block the next model family. Unknown roles are legal.

kind.description: `runtime_carry` is a value arriving from a previous invocation -- not an intra-step cycle, which is what distinguishes a legal carry from an inverted residual.

invocation_offset.description: For kind=runtime_carry: how many invocations back the value came from.

source_ref.description: file:line where this edge is visible. Required: an edge with no source line cannot be checked against the source, which is the only thing that can prove it.

component_groups.description: Repeated component stacks, as a general alternative to `architecture.layer_groups`. Lets a model have several stacks, or a stack that is not the single decoder chain layer_groups assumes. Optional and additive: layer_groups stays valid for the single-stack case.

definition.description: The structure key each repetition instantiates.

sharing.description: Whether repetitions share weights. `unknown` is legal; guessing is not, because it changes what a per-layer cost means.

structures.description: Representative structure tree per layer_group type / stage. Keyed by type name.

excluded_profiler_ops.description: Ops legitimately excluded from model/runtime accounting: profiler/bookkeeping only. reason_code MUST be from the finite enum and MUST carry evidence. Main-compute kernels (MatMul/Attention/Norm/MoE/comm/Gather/KVcache/sampling) may NEVER appear here.

unmapped_ops.description: Ops with UNKNOWN ownership — mapping is incomplete. Strict validation FAILS if this is non-empty. A free-text reason does NOT make an op 'covered'; only explicit model/runtime/excluded ownership does.

node.description: One node of a structure tree. `children` expresses CONTAINMENT ONLY: adjacency in that list is not a dataflow edge, so residuals and parallel paths belong in `branches`.

architecture_group_type.description: For a top-level runtime template, the learned architecture.layer_groups/prediction_modules type that owns it. A capture may have multiple runtime templates with one learned owner.

runtime_pattern.description: Capture-specific template identity. It is not a learned layer type and must not create an architecture group.

shape_semantic.description: OPTIONAL shape annotation. Also legal on a kernel; `validate_shapes.py` reads both. Not part of the formal contract -- its absence says nothing about whether the decomposition is right (run_validation.py --with-shapes).

op_data.description: Raw profiler rows for this node's ops, keyed by `index`, used by validate_shapes.py to check declared shapes against measured dims. Debugging aid, not contract.

org_index.description: Row position in the unfiltered profiler export, so a row stays traceable after filtering.

shape_raw.description: Unparsed shape text as the profiler emitted it, kept beside the split forms so a parse failure stays inspectable.

stream_id.description: String, not integer: profiler exports carry it as text.

parallel_siblings.description: Groups of this node's children that consume the same producer instead of feeding each other. Declared here because `build_architecture_graph.py` reads it: while it was absent from this schema it could be neither required nor validated, which is the exact hole `additionalProperties: false` closes. `children` order alone reads as a chain, so an undeclared fan-out renders as the wrong topology. Prefer a `branches` entry with kind=parallel, which also names where the paths fork and rejoin; this field records only that the members are siblings.

members.description: Child names that run in parallel. Fewer than two is not a fan-out.

kernel.description: One profiler op attributed to this node. Was previously an unconstrained object, so a misspelled `shape_semantic` silently read as absent.

shape_semantic.description: OPTIONAL annotation layered on the profiler's dims. Not part of the formal contract: its absence says nothing about whether the decomposition is right (see run_validation.py --with-shapes).

branch.description: A non-chain edge between two nodes of the same structure. `children` expresses containment ONLY -- adjacency in that list is not a dataflow edge -- so every residual, every parallel path and every skip must appear here or it does not exist downstream. `inputs` names where the path forks off and `output` where it rejoins; the siblings strictly between them are what it bypasses. Endpoints may be bare child names or fully-qualified node ids.

kind.description: Omitted means `residual`, matching what every consumer already assumes.

source_ref.description: file:line where this edge is visible in forward(). A branch without one cannot be checked against the source, which is the only thing that can prove it. `code_ref` is accepted as the equivalent spelling, since structure nodes use that name.

invocation_offset.description: For kind=cross_invocation: how many invocations back the carried value came from. A residual entering a repeated block from its own previous invocation is NOT an intra-block cycle, and this is what distinguishes the two.

execution_profile.description: One deployment configuration of the same source: which forward method each component actually runs, and which config-gated arms were selected. Two profiles (prefill/decode, quantised/not) may share component definitions while activating different subgraphs.

selected_variants.description: Which arm of each config-gated branch this profile takes. Recorded rather than inferred: the extractor can see both arms but not which one a deployment chose.
